newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil up, contango narrows.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil up, contango narrows.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps was firm at midday on Thursday rising for the fourth day in a row on expectations of fresh demand from China and short covering, traders said.
The unexpected strength of the swaps front month and the prompt physical market has narrowed the inter-front month spread.
August swaps were last quoted at $22.75/$22.90 per barrel, up about 30 cents from Tuesday's $22.40/$22.50 per barrel, brokers said.
September was last quoted at $23.35/$23.50, from Tuesday's $23.10/$23.20.
As a result, the August/September narrowed to trade earlier in the day at minus 50 cents from an early week traded level of minus 70 cents, brokers said.
Traders said the swaps strength was triggered by buying interests from China and a major late last week when prices fell to $21.50 per barrel where these companies came in to buy in force.
That buying spree led to prices rising to around $22.00 per barrel before a new round of buying from players looking to cover short sales raised prices further to around $22.40 on Wednesday.
At the same time, physical purchases in the spot market also gave fresh impetus to the bull run.
Physical buyers were continually bidding and purchasing at higher prices.
On Wednesday, one 150,000-barrel cargo for August 7-10 lifting traded at $21.90 per barrel, up $1.00 from Monday's lowest traded level.
On Monday, four deals totalling 670,000 barrels were done between $20.90 and $21.20 per barrel on a free-on-board Singapore basis.
The fuel oil market was steady with August last quoted at $98.75/$99.50, brokers said.
